# Painted arena: shared 2.5D production reference

**Latest map:** owner requested the painting become a larger playable battlefield. `painted-valley-v2` is 2600×1440 with a ~400-unit middle lane and relocated jungle camps; see [map authority, artwork and verification](playable-valley.md). The initial preview/background-only assumptions below are historical for this map.

**Latest:** Owner subsequently requested live integration, arena first and then Mirelle. Painted ground/scenery and two-facing Mirelle are now the default limited live presentation in Babylon matches and replay. This supersedes the preview-only staging below for these assets. Read [live integration](live-integration.md) for exact files, checks and remaining quality limits. The original `/arena-2d.html` remains an isolated art inspection page.

Owner decision, 2026-10-24: try detailed painted 2.5D art and animations in Babylon.js, preserving every avatar's identity. The owner explicitly approved a **separate painted-sprite workflow with its own animation checks**. The 3D clean-base/rig pipeline and its failed candidates retain their status. This approval permits new sprite illustrations; it does not qualify or publish them.

## Trial and ownership

`/root` owns the new arena painting, Mirelle sprite sheet, isolated Babylon preview and this reference. No delegated agents. Open `/arena-2d.html` on the existing Vite development server. For a separate static build run `npx vite build --config vite.arena2d.config.ts` in `EsportsClash.Web`; serve `arena-2d-dist` over HTTP. The usual production app build does not include the trial page.

The trial is an art playback laboratory, not a playable combat mode. It offers Idle, Run, Cast and Death, pause, frame stepping, speed, two stitch geometry studies and all 45 identity/ability references. Selecting another identity changes reference text only. One generated Mirelle atlas contains sixteen draft keyframes; it is not 45 finished animated characters. The environment is a concept painting with baked scenery, not collision-aligned terrain. No publication, match renderer switch, API mutation, legacy asset restoration, simulation, AI or frozen ML changes.

## Sources and precedence

Use `src/data/heroIdentityV3.json` for canonical and persisted IDs; `src/data/v3RosterDesign.json` for original art, signatures, counterplay, P/S1/S2/R and Mirelle's ten pages. The generated [roster reference](roster-reference.md) preserves these current briefs and links their source hashes. Do not use the historical October 23 ability catalog or removed model binaries as fresh art sources. Published registry data and the active match snapshot may supersede bundled presentation fields. Executable handlers in `v3Combat.ts`, `v3Roster.ts`, `v3Arena.ts` and event snapshots determine actual geometry/timing/damage, not prose cooldowns.

Some historical anatomy descriptions conflict with the new identity briefs (for example nine tails versus Mireth's one-tail description). Flag these before producing that character; do not silently merge them or change the 3D anatomy registry. Preserve stable IDs, species, age, body proportions, handedness, companions, weapons and distinct visual motifs. Never turn the whole roster into human mages or copy the old names/abilities back.

## Art direction

Detailed painted fantasy, strong silhouettes, textured stone and cloth, restrained luminous accents. Teal and coral sanctuary colors supplement shape/team markers. The combat lane stays quieter than the perimeter; avoid high-contrast ground ornament under telegraphs. Fix the camera, ground baseline, shadow direction and apparent character scale. Keep anatomy, face, outfit fasteners and equipment consistent across frames. Do not mirror asymmetric equipment as a substitute for drawing the opposite facing. Keep ground shadows, character, weapon trails, status marks and effect geometry in separate layers in production.

Mirelle: adult atelier mage, needle comb, ink-black asymmetrical sleeve, ivory waistcoat, oxblood petal skirt over shorts, flat boots, paper-pattern cape, brass bobbin. Pin placement is a precise needle flick; Recut pulls a tensioned thread; page selection opens a pattern fan. No elemental orb recipes, meteor, EMP or elemental familiar. The generated bobbin currently reads too much like a circular ornament; refine its spool silhouette. The sheet's cape and sleeve consistency and cast-trail padding also require review.

## Animation production contract

| Motion | Initial production target per direction | Required review |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Idle | 8 frames, 8 fps, loop | Stable planted feet, modest breathing, no accumulating drift |
| Walk / Run | 8 / 12 frames, 10 / 12 fps, loop | Alternating contacts, speed tied to snapshot velocity; no baked travel |
| Basic attack | 8 frames, event-driven | Anticipation, authoritative release marker, recoil, recover |
| S1 / S2 / R | 8–12 distinct frames each | Character-specific gesture; event timing; interrupt/recovery transition |
| Hit | 4 frames, non-loop | Additive recoil must not conceal attack or imply new stun |
| Death | 10 frames, non-loop | Collapse reaches ground, terminal frame held, effects expire |
| Spawn / victory | 8 frames each | Presentation only; respects alive/dead state |

Start with eight authored directions, four only for an explicitly limited trial. Draw rear views; never billboard a front view through a freely orbiting camera. Current trial has one right-facing view and four frames each for Idle/Run/Cast/Death. The generated run poses need a stronger opposing stride; four images alone do not establish a seamless gait. No interpolation can invent missing limb poses.

Each atlas manifest must include schema version, avatar ID, asset epoch, source/prompt hash, file SHA-256, width/height, alpha, cell rectangles, per-frame foot pivot, animation order/durations/loop flag, direction, bounds and release/recovery markers. Use trimmed rectangles with 2–4 pixels of extruded padding for production; share texture resources across instances. Nearest cell-grid sampling in this draft still requires a boundary/bleed audit. Approximate memory: a 2048-square RGBA atlas is 16 MiB before mipmaps, about 21.3 MiB with them; load selected match characters only and measure actual GPU use.

## Abilities and VFX

For every slot use the roster reference's exact name and effect brief. Author four layers: (1) source-character gesture, (2) ground-space warning with directional/shape cues, (3) active projectile/construct/impact, (4) readable expiry or destruction. Hostile warning and safe gaps must remain readable without color. Distinguish preview from active area with dashed versus solid borders. Effects cannot expand hitboxes, hide counterplay, reset cooldowns or cause damage.

Mirelle's passive renders up to three independently targetable pins with public lifetime/health cues. S1 shows a pin's flight and actual landing; S2 shows the valid slide route and warning before moving the pin. R uses the selected named page's geometry and consumed-pin events. Baste Line is an open-ended stitched seam, not a solid wall. Grand Atelier unfolds a canopy after its warning, keeps combatants visible and collapses on the authoritative support event. The trial's static seam/triangle are visual vocabulary studies, not validated runtime abilities. See the ten complete page briefs in the roster reference; each needs separate VFX and counterplay review.

All other avatars need equally specific attacks and slot motions: shields visibly rotate with their facing, forks anchor to endpoints, companions animate independently, vehicles retain their footprint, tails and wings follow their owner's anatomy. Copying Mirelle's cast onto everyone fails identity review. Do not render decorative danger zones where the runtime has no threat.

## Babylon integration plan

1. Qualify Mirelle's sprite identity, alignment, gait and all required directions before a live renderer experiment.
2. Add an explicit opt-in presentation mode consuming copied `ArenaFrame`/`ViewerActor` snapshots. Keep existing simulation authority, selection, ground coordinates, collision and HUD unchanged.
3. Use a fixed orthographic camera and planes/sprite atlas UVs with foot pivots, world depth, alpha-tested edges and correctly ordered translucent VFX. Terrain elevation affects the ground anchor. Actor motion derives from snapshot time, not wall-clock time; pause/seek/replay and 1x/4x must agree.
4. Rebuild the painted environment in terrain-aligned floor tiles plus foreground cutouts. Fade occluders near actors; retain hitbox and telegraph visibility. The concept image cannot replace collision geography directly.
5. Test three unlike body plans before scaling to 45: Mirelle, a creature and a companion/vehicle character. Then deliver in roster batches with identity and ability evidence, never blanket qualification.

## Gates for every agent

Read this file, current handoff, character pipeline and mechanics first. Declare owned files/stage. Consume only exact asset IDs/hashes, preserve failed evidence, record revisions separately, and message adjacent active agents or leave handoff notes here. No asset becomes production-ready because PNG loading or TypeScript succeeds.

Review alpha on light/dark backgrounds; cell boundaries, foot pivots, missing limbs, silhouette at match scale, eight directions, frame transitions, cast timing, terminal Death, companion consistency, safe gaps, depth sorting, occlusion, reduced motion and 10-actor performance. Verify pause/seek and context recovery. Run game checks/build for integration work. Record actual browser screenshots and limitations. Final publication requires explicit qualification through the existing release controls.

Next unresolved stage: refine Mirelle's four-frame draft into consistent, pivot-aligned production motion and author other directions; develop runtime-bound ability effects and terrain-aligned environment layers. No production qualification is claimed.

## Solenne Vaelor — The Sunwall Oath

Stable ID: `c_solana`. Canonical ID: `solenne-vaelor`. Role: protector / angular defense.

**Appearance:** battle-scarred sun knight with a tall hinged heliograph shield; ivory-bronze armor, burnt-red sash, mechanical iris on the shield

**Combat identity:** turns *facing and coverage* into a teamfight resource.

**Readable counterplay:** take side angles, destroy the panel with two projectile impacts, or force her to protect the wrong flank.

Animation planning: preserve this silhouette in Idle/Run/Attack/Hit/Death. Author a separate gesture, telegraph, active effect and expiry for each slot below; synchronize the production result to authoritative events. All artwork/motion remains unqualified until reviewed.

### P: Earned Daylight

blocking hostile damage with the front 110° of her shield stocks up to 3 Radiance (1 stack / 3 s). No free stacks for standing still.

Design cooldown note: passive / no cooldown specified. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S1: Sun Dial

stakes a 70-GU-wide oriented shield panel for 3.5 s. Intercepts the first two hostile projectiles that cross its front; melee units pass. Opponents may walk around it.

Design cooldown note: 9 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S2: Pivot Order

rotates an existing panel up to 100° or, if none exists, rotates Solenne's personal guard and advances 38 GU; Radiance spent gives adjacent allies a 1.5 s directional damage reduction against attacks coming from the chosen side.

Design cooldown note: 12 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### R: Noon Divide

from her current panel, projects two slowly separating sunbeams for 4 s, creating a wide **protected wedge**. Allies inside gain 18% damage mitigation from outside; enemies inside can still fight. Spending 3 Radiance gives 1 brief shove at initial expansion (not a mass stun).

Design cooldown note: 85 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

## Ivera Frostwhistle — The Frost Resonant

Stable ID: `c_astra`. Canonical ID: `ivera-frostwhistle`. Role: marksman / echo geometry.

**Appearance:** tall northern bow engineer wearing permafrost string gauges and layered ice-tuning plates; asymmetric longbow bearing vibrating crystal forks

**Combat identity:** makes **resonant frost strings**, not auto-attack slow stacks.

**Readable counterplay:** smash one fork, enter through gaps, or attack while Ivera is placing geometry.

Animation planning: preserve this silhouette in Idle/Run/Attack/Hit/Death. Author a separate gesture, telegraph, active effect and expiry for each slot below; synchronize the production result to authoritative events. All artwork/motion remains unqualified until reviewed.

### P: Overtone

landing a aimed shot temporarily tunes a visible location, maximum 2, each persisting 5 s. Shots do not globally slow.

Design cooldown note: passive / no cooldown specified. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S1: Tuning Shot

fires a narrow bolt that installs a crystal fork at its endpoint (terrain or ground); fork has 2 hit points. Can be fired through a champion for light damage, but ends behind them.

Design cooldown note: 8 s, two charges. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S2: Singing Ice

activates a frost vibration along the line between the two newest forks for 3 s. Enemies *crossing* the line suffer 28% slow for 1.1 s and take one burst; allies firing **parallel** to the line gain a small projectile-speed bonus.

Design cooldown note: 14 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### R: Glass Rapture

resonates all active forks in a broad triangular sound field. Over 1.2 s the field forms three visible safe gaps; enemies still on the sounding lines take high damage and a 0.55 s stagger. Consumes forks.

Design cooldown note: 80 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

## Mireth Lune — The Witness of False Roads

Stable ID: `c_kyumi`. Canonical ID: `mireth-lune`. Role: route deception mage.

**Appearance:** austere one-tailed fox archivist in deep blue-gray traveling robes with glass route tablets; no alluring charm trope

**Combat identity:** makes an enemy's *chosen route* risky, without mind control.

**Readable counterplay:** vary approach headings, ignore the tempting doorway, destroy it with attacks.

Animation planning: preserve this silhouette in Idle/Run/Attack/Hit/Death. Author a separate gesture, telegraph, active effect and expiry for each slot below; synchronize the production result to authoritative events. All artwork/motion remains unqualified until reviewed.

### P: Witness Marks

after an enemy moves 70 GU while visible to Mireth, records its heading as a glowing arrow for 3 s, once per enemy / 6 s.

Design cooldown note: passive / no cooldown specified. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S1: Counterpath

draws a short luminous road across an observed heading. Crossing it in the recorded direction costs 25% move speed for 1 s; crossing opposite grants no penalty. Can be skirted.

Design cooldown note: 8 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S2: False Exit

places a glass doorway that visually points to safety but openly projects its **actual** exit 75 GU to one side. The first enemy who voluntarily enters is displaced to that endpoint after 0.35 s. Enemy sees both endpoints before entering; no forced input manipulation.

Design cooldown note: 13 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### R: Map of Might-Have-Beens

shows up to three recorded headings as public spectral roads for 4 s; allies gain speed while traversing them opposite the recorded direction, and foes crossing in the old direction receive a short revealed/exposed mark. No auto charm, orb return, or dash chain.

Design cooldown note: 83 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

## Bramm Coil — The Breach Marshal

Stable ID: `c_buck`. Canonical ID: `bramm-coil`. Role: anti-cover artillery / knockline specialist.

**Appearance:** industrial tunnel-breaker with rotary ram-gun mounted to a back brace, orange work stripes and one reinforced leg

**Combat identity:** generates **controlled breach lanes**, not shotgun pellet bursts or smoke obscuration.

**Readable counterplay:** relocate laterally, interrupt his bracing, attack his exposed back.

Animation planning: preserve this silhouette in Idle/Run/Attack/Hit/Death. Author a separate gesture, telegraph, active effect and expiry for each slot below; synchronize the production result to authoritative events. All artwork/motion remains unqualified until reviewed.

### P: Structural Survey

repeated hits on the same piece of deployable cover mark it as weakened (maximum one mark).

Design cooldown note: passive / no cooldown specified. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S1: Anchor Ram

shoots a riveted anchor 140 GU to a ground point. After 0.6 s the anchor pushes a rectangular 45×90-GU blast **away from its own facing**; hits one time, moves enemies 24 GU, dislodges deployable barriers.

Design cooldown note: 9 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S2: Brace Exchange

Bramm exchanges mobility for steadiness for 3 s. He slows by 25%; each shot fired from the brace creates a short **safe opening** in allied cover that closes after 0.7 s, permitting planned fire without permanently destroying shields.

Design cooldown note: 13 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### R: Tunnel Cut

slowly draws a huge visible straight cutting lane for 1.1 s. It then advances a mechanical ram through the lane over 1.4 s, collapsing temporary structures and forcing units sideways to the nearest free side; never passes world walls.

Design cooldown note: 76 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

## Kael Vespera — The Oath Ledger

Stable ID: `c_valkira`. Canonical ID: `kael-vespera`. Role: anti-save fighter / wager duelist.

**Appearance:** weathered oath collector with paired crescent ledgers as blades, stitched gray cape and ink-red wrist seals

**Combat identity:** enforces a transparent **risk bargain** on one enemy instead of leaping for an execute.

**Readable counterplay:** assign a defender to pressure Kael; avoid shielding into her Contract without reason.

Animation planning: preserve this silhouette in Idle/Run/Attack/Hit/Death. Author a separate gesture, telegraph, active effect and expiry for each slot below; synchronize the production result to authoritative events. All artwork/motion remains unqualified until reviewed.

### P: Outstanding Balance

first melee contact with a hero issues a visible 4 s Contract: target receives a 4% damage discount from Kael, but each shield granted during the Contract accumulates *Debt* (capped at 160). Only Kael may collect; no denial of healing.

Design cooldown note: passive / no cooldown specified. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S1: Collection Line

short sweeping arc which draws a red boundary on the ground for 2 s. Contracted targets crossing it pay a fraction of Debt as magic damage; staying put avoids payment.

Design cooldown note: 7 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S2: Witness Required

Kael braces for 0.8 s. If the contracted enemy or a defender hits her during the brace, she gains a dashless counter slash and a 1 s damage reduction; otherwise she is vulnerable after bracing.

Design cooldown note: 13 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### R: Terms of Mercy

challenges a contracted target for 4 s. Their team can clear the Contract by landing two attacks on Kael, or ignore it and let Kael cash out accrued Debt as a single capped hit. Does not suppress, force 1v1, or execute automatically.

Design cooldown note: 80 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

## Nyxara Vale — The Silhouette Thief

Stable ID: `c_kage`. Canonical ID: `nyxara-vale`. Role: vision-pressure assassin.

**Appearance:** angular thief wearing articulated matte-black lacquer strips that cast sharp, oversized silhouettes on the ground; no shadow clones

**Combat identity:** manipulates **the edges of visibility**.

**Readable counterplay:** sweep close vision across the veil, stand back-to-back, shoot area spells into silhouette arcs.

Animation planning: preserve this silhouette in Idle/Run/Attack/Hit/Death. Author a separate gesture, telegraph, active effect and expiry for each slot below; synchronize the production result to authoritative events. All artwork/motion remains unqualified until reviewed.

### P: Blind Side

Nyxara gains a small first-hit bonus when striking from outside the target's *forward* vision cone, once / target / 7 s. Visible directional marker informs defenders when exposed.

Design cooldown note: passive / no cooldown specified. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S1: Shadow Pin

projects a dark triangular plane from a chosen wall or her own location for 4 s. It blocks **line of sight for basic attack acquisition**, not projectiles, and is transparent to all after a unit steps through.

Design cooldown note: 8 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S2: Light Theft

steals illumination from one existing Shadow Pin for 2 s, collapsing that plane into a mobile veil around Nyxara. She remains targetable at close range and leaves bright footsteps; while veiled, her next attack briefly reduces the victim's turn speed.

Design cooldown note: 13 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### R: Total Eclipse, Partial Truth

places three visible *false target silhouettes* along an 80-GU arc. They do not attack, teleport, or explode; enemy targeting systems briefly need fresh line-of-sight confirmation when Nyxara crosses the arc. Her next hit against an isolated foe deals bonus damage, capped.

Design cooldown note: 85 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

## Serrin Galecrest — The Crosswind Cartographer

Stable ID: `c_kazemaru`. Canonical ID: `serrin-galecrest`. Role: projectile-lane engineer / duelist.

**Appearance:** white-haired sailor swordsman with a collapsible wind vane shield and narrow curved blade; weather-map tapes attached to armor

**Combat identity:** changes **wind vectors** rather than summoning tornadoes or airborne execution.

**Readable counterplay:** use melee pressure, homing attacks, or reposition before firing.

Animation planning: preserve this silhouette in Idle/Run/Attack/Hit/Death. Author a separate gesture, telegraph, active effect and expiry for each slot below; synchronize the production result to authoritative events. All artwork/motion remains unqualified until reviewed.

### P: Weather Reading

Serrin sees recent incoming projectile headings as faint arrows; after narrowly dodging one, gains one Wind Notch (max 2).

Design cooldown note: passive / no cooldown specified. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S1: Compass Slash

cuts a 65-GU directional current across a target corridor for 2.2 s. Enemy **non-homing** projectiles crossing it are deflected up to 15°; allied shots get a 10% speed boost.

Design cooldown note: 7 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S2: Tack Change

spends a Wind Notch to rotate a current or quickly sidestep 28 GU perpendicular to its path. Cannot pass hard terrain.

Design cooldown note: 12 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

maps a 140-GU radius ring with four public directional wind channels for 4 s. Enemy projectile lanes become less reliable; walking normally still works. No blanket projectile deletion, knockup, or blink slashes.

Design cooldown note: 88 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

## Orin and Fen — Keepers of the Last Lantern

Stable ID: `c_kindra`. Canonical ID: `orin-and-fen`. Role: scouting marksman / extraction support.

**Appearance:** scarred human lantern scout followed by a blind, horned dusk-hound made of moving ember fur; **not** a wolf plus death-immunity circle

**Combat identity:** tracks danger and guides **one wounded ally out**.

**Readable counterplay:** attack the lantern, attack from non-projectile angles, or force the rescued ally off the route.

Animation planning: preserve this silhouette in Idle/Run/Attack/Hit/Death. Author a separate gesture, telegraph, active effect and expiry for each slot below; synchronize the production result to authoritative events. All artwork/motion remains unqualified until reviewed.

### P: Scent of Trouble

Fen marks heroes who recently damaged Orin's allies, revealing their direction for 3 s (not through fog beyond a short final ping).

Design cooldown note: passive / no cooldown specified. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S1: Track Lantern

Orin drops a lantern that records the next enemy who passes within 55 GU, pinging their direction; can be destroyed in 2 hits.

Design cooldown note: 9 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S2: Fen, Guard

sends Fen to a chosen ally or lantern for 3 s. Fen absorbs the next **one** eligible hostile projectile and then withdraws, with a clearly visible charge indicator.

Design cooldown note: 14 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

paints a luminous curved **retreat path** from Orin to one low-HP ally for 4 s. The selected ally may voluntarily follow it for 30% speed and 18% damage reduction while moving toward Orin; leaving the path cancels protection. No HP floor or mass invulnerability.

Design cooldown note: 90 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

## Quillene Rook — The Sky Loom Fletcher

Stable ID: `c_cora`. Canonical ID: `quillene-rook`. Role: ranged interception carry.

**Appearance:** masked archer with hawk-inspired shoulder fins and bow strung with miniature kite rigging; feathers are **air anchors**, not returning blade traps

**Combat identity:** creates temporary **crossfire windows**.

**Readable counterplay:** pop the kites or enter close combat beneath the span.

Animation planning: preserve this silhouette in Idle/Run/Attack/Hit/Death. Author a separate gesture, telegraph, active effect and expiry for each slot below; synchronize the production result to authoritative events. All artwork/motion remains unqualified until reviewed.

### P: Airborne Fletching

every third aimed attack releases a tiny kite that hangs for 3 s at the shot's endpoint (max 3). Kites are visible and destroyable.

Design cooldown note: passive / no cooldown specified. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S1: Tetherbolt

shoots a kite anchor 150 GU into the air; anchors do not damage when planted.

Design cooldown note: 8 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

ties her two nearest kites into an aerial span for 3 s. Her next two arrows passing through it split into two shallow angled shots at 60% damage each (one-hit cap per target); enemy units may shoot down either kite.

Design cooldown note: 13 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### R: Harrier Net

all active kites fan into a broad descending mesh. Enemies inside may move out but have ranged attack windups increased for 2.5 s; meanwhile allied projectiles from outside the mesh get a slight side-angle adjustment. No untargetable leap, ground feather recall, or root-on-three-feathers.

Design cooldown note: 85 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

## Aurelio Vane — The Masquerade Marshal

Stable ID: `c_renn`. Canonical ID: `aurelio-vane`. Role: formation choreographer / rescue.

**Appearance:** masked fencing host in ceremonial midnight tux-armor with luminous floorwork slippers and half-moon fan shield

**Combat identity:** gives allies **explicit dance steps** instead of dash-and-charm engagement.

**Readable counterplay:** block a turn or attack the side where the next step ends.

Animation planning: preserve this silhouette in Idle/Run/Attack/Hit/Death. Author a separate gesture, telegraph, active effect and expiry for each slot below; synchronize the production result to authoritative events. All artwork/motion remains unqualified until reviewed.

### P: Perfect Partner

an ally who follows an Aurelio-created floor arrow gains brief tenacity, once / ally / 6 s.

Design cooldown note: passive / no cooldown specified. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S1: Mark the Floor

lays two 30-GU glowing steps; an ally crossing them in order gains 22% movement speed for 1.5 s. Enemies see the steps and can deny the route.

selects an allied hero in 120 GU; for 1.2 s both can voluntarily trade their places by pressing an interaction or by an AI commitment. Cannot trade into walls or out of hard CC.

reveals a three-turn floor route for 4 s. Allies following it earn a small shield at each turn; enemies who stand on the route are pushed sideways 18 GU once when the procession advances. No AoE charm or automatic ally dash.

## Droven Bearmantle — The Keeper of the Second Heart

Stable ID: `c_sylla`. Canonical ID: `droven-bearmantle`. Role: two-body defender / attrition.

**Appearance:** rugged warden in patched antlered mantle accompanied by a massive **moss-backed pack tortoise**, not a spirit bear or shapeshifter

**Combat identity:** a slow second body that redistributes pressure.

**Readable counterplay:** hit Droven when guard moves away, attack shell from side, or use area damage around the tortoise.

Animation planning: preserve this silhouette in Idle/Run/Attack/Hit/Death. Author a separate gesture, telegraph, active effect and expiry for each slot below; synchronize the production result to authoritative events. All artwork/motion remains unqualified until reviewed.

### P: Shared Heartbeat

Droven and the tortoise Hark have a shared reserve of 220 guard energy; damage absorbed by Hark drains guard. Hark does not respawn instantly after destruction.

Design cooldown note: passive / no cooldown specified. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

### S1: Hark, Settle

directs Hark to a nearby point where he plants as a 55-GU-wide **walk-around obstacle** for 4 s. Hark can be attacked; allies may pass through slowly.

Hark opens his shell to cover one nearby ally with 20% incoming-damage redirection to guard energy for 2.5 s. Droven temporarily loses part of his own armor while energy is transferred.

Design cooldown note: 14 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

Hark slowly advances 100 GU over 4 s as moving cover. Allies behind his shell gain limited projectile protection; opponents can flank Hark or destroy the shell's guard energy.

Design cooldown note: 92 s. Check executable runtime before timing VFX.

## Thalara Rootwright — The Mycelial Architect

Stable ID: `c_tequoia`. Canonical ID: `thalara-rootwright`. Role: ground economy / area control.

**Appearance:** elderly fungus architect with ceramic seed jars, branching mycelium sleeves and mushroom-coral parasol; no tree-ring prison

**Combat identity:** grows **networks with limited nutrient supply**.

**Readable counterplay:** sever key nodes or force the fight beyond the nutrient network.

Animation planning: preserve this silhouette in Idle/Run/Attack/Hit/Death. Author a separate gesture, telegraph, active effect and expiry for each slot below; synchronize the production result to authoritative events. All artwork/motion remains unqualified until reviewed.

### P: Spores in Soil

ability hits leave a nutrient node for 6 s (max 4). Nodes are visible small mushrooms with 2 hit points.

# EsportsClash — Babylon.js 9 migration plan

**Edition:** 2026-10-23  
**Decision:** Babylon.js 9 (renderer and presentation), React + Vite + TypeScript + VS Code + Codex, while retaining a renderer-independent authoritative combat simulation and the existing Laravel backend.

> Design and migration guidance, **not an implementation**. Exact repository layout and current renderer remain unverified; Codex must inspect the real repository before creating directories, installing packages, or replacing components.

## Authoritative existing specifications

Read these source files before any code changes:

1. `ESPORTSCLASH_ORIGINAL_45_HERO_REDESIGN_V3.md` — canonical V3 characters and effects.
2. `ESPORTSCLASH_V3_ABILITY_DESIGN_MANIFEST.json` — editorial machine-readable V3 kit inventory; not runtime code.
3. `ESPORTSCLASH_V3_ENGINE_AI_BALANCE.md` — fixed-step combat, AI, and runtime acceptance contracts.
4. `ESPORTSCLASH_V3_CHARACTER_ART_BIBLE.md` — visual and rigging targets.
5. `ESPORTSCLASH_CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_MASTER_PROMPT_V3.md` — earlier combat/ability implementation guide; this migration plan adds renderer-specific constraints.

**Do not use the older avatar catalog, V1 rename file, or V2 teamfight redesign as the new source of truth.** Keep old IDs stable; introduce display-name/canonical-name aliases, not destructive primary-key rewrites.

## Why Babylon.js 9

- TypeScript-first npm modules run directly in Vite from VS Code, without mandatory visual editor.
- Mature scene/lighting/materials/GUI/particle/animation capabilities for a camera-driven browser MOBA.
- Babylon.js 9 `AnimatorAvatar.retargetAnimationGroup` provides skeleton and rest-pose aware retargeting where the source data supports it; validate bone naming, hierarchy, reference pose, root motion and foot contact. It is **not** an automatic rig quality fixer.
- glTF 2.0 / `.glb` models integrate with the animation/VFX pipeline. Code can own the entire scene lifecycle.
- React remains for HUD, spectator controls, cards, match UX. Integrate a Babylon `<canvas>` as one imperative React component, not a second React-based 3D scene graph.

Tradeoffs: more renderer/animation wiring than a turnkey visual editor; Babylon is not inherently faster than PlayCanvas. Profile **WebGL2 and WebGPU** on representative content before final cutover. PlayCanvas remains the fallback if rendering budgets fail; don't overgeneralize synthetic benchmarks.

## Adapter contract

The simulation advances by fixed **simulation ticks**, never by rendering delta time. Browser rendering is a one-way consumer of authorized state/snapshots/events.

```ts
type Tick = number;
type ActorId = string;

type CombatEvent =
  | { kind: 'cast_started'; tick: Tick; casterId: ActorId; abilityId: string; castId: string }
  | { kind: 'cast_committed'; tick: Tick; casterId: ActorId; abilityId: string; castId: string }
  | { kind: 'damage_applied'; tick: Tick; sourceId: ActorId; targetId: ActorId; amount: number }
  | { kind: 'construct_spawned'; tick: Tick; constructId: string; constructType: string }
  | { kind: 'construct_destroyed'; tick: Tick; constructId: string }
  | { kind: 'status_applied'; tick: Tick; targetId: ActorId; statusId: string };

interface SimulationSnapshot {
  tick: Tick;
  actors: Array<{ id: ActorId; heroId: string; x: number; y: number; facingRad: number; hp: number; alive: boolean }>;
  constructs: Array<{ id: string; type: string; x: number; y: number }>;
  stateHash: string;
}

interface MatchViewer {
  mount(canvas: HTMLCanvasElement): Promise<void>;
  loadSnapshot(snapshot: SimulationSnapshot): void;
  receiveEvents(events: CombatEvent[]): void;
  setPlaybackRate(rate: 1 | 2 | 4): void;
  dispose(): void;
}
```

**Conceptual schema only.** Extend based on the actual V3 effect spec and event log, prefer existing typed events if present, and define authoritative types once. Rendering may interpolate between immutable snapshots but MUST NOT resolve hits, manage cooldowns, or issue AI decisions. If locally generated particle randomness is used, it must never affect simulation randomness. Implement authoritative spatial queries, projectile collision, temporary cover, player consent, and hazard durations in the simulation, not Babylon/Havok.

- Create an isolated branch and feature flag (`viewer=babylon|legacy`).
- Inspect actual rendering stack; map imports of rendering APIs, combat state, physics, animation, camera, asset loaders, and AI runtime.
- Run baseline unit/e2e tests and a seeded match at 1× and 4×, saving input log + result hash + replay.

- Build an animation state machine with wind-up/commit/recovery driven by **simulation event timestamps**. Animation may react but must not decide combat events.

### Gate 4 — Replay, headless AI, time dilation

- Keep headless trainer free of Babylon, DOM, WebGL, WebGPU, and mesh dependencies.
- Make 4× an advancement policy over the SAME fixed-size ticks, not a quadrupled delta. Time stamps, cooldowns, duration and seeded RNG must be invariant.
- Implement event-log + periodic snapshot replay, seek, pause and speed controls in viewer only.
- Match 1× and 4× result hashes for same policy version/seed/action log. Verify that rendering 30/60/144 fps doesn't change outcomes.

### Gate 5 — 45-avatar migration

- Add `legacyId -> canonical identity` alias mapping; preserve saved cards and past results.
- Read the V3 machine-readable roster and verify exactly 45 IDs, 180 base slots and ten Mirelle pages; validate runtime effects independently of text.
- Migrate five-avatar test set first, remaining groups thereafter, with replay-based behavioral acceptance tests and AI ability usage checks.
- Reject a kit if only a tooltip/VFX changed; verify mechanics at the simulation layer.
- **Go when:** all characters load with unique identity and supported model fallback, all ability mechanics pass tests, no forbidden old copied kit silently restored.

### Gate 6 — Optimize / cut over

- Benchmark representative ten-avatar teamfights (regular and worst-case ability overlap) at 1080p, measure FPS p50/p1, GPU/CPU frame time, JS heap, VRAM where available, network/asset payload and shader compile stalls.
- Candidate **initial desktop target**, not a measured claim: stable 60 fps for a normal ten-avatar fight on the chosen baseline system; evaluate a lower-quality 30 fps fallback. Check both WebGL2 and WebGPU; choose whichever performs better per browser/device.
- Reduce draw calls and materials; pool VFX; prewarm frequent shaders; LOD and texture compression; asynchronously load skins and rare avatar assets. Never degrade authoritative simulation accuracy to gain frames.
- Roll out legacy/Babylon viewer feature flag; monitor errors and visual regressions; retain rollback until production parity verified.
- **Go when:** no material regression in match outcomes, load latency and stability are acceptable, rollback documented.

## Major risks and mitigations

1. **Rendering physics hijacks combat:** enforce one-way data flow and static import boundaries.
2. **Rigged assets look broken:** add model validation, reference pose adjustment and targeted offline correction; retargeting is not a substitute for good weights/topology.
3. **WebGPU unexpectedly slower on a particular browser:** runtime backend selection and WebGL2 fallback, profile actual game content.
4. **Breaking persistent cards due to renames:** stable legacy key and migration fixtures.
5. **Codex tries to implement all 45 at once:** milestone PRs; insist on tests and measurable gates before scope expansion.
6. **V3 design confused with executable code:** require working effect handlers and real matches, not just manifest updates.
